chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:

I asked him about the sick person who becomes unconscious and then regains consciousness. How does he make up his prayer? He said: He makes up the prayer for the time at which he regained consciousness.
ai.seo_question: How does a patient make up missed prayers after regaining consciousness following unconsciousness?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of 'ghafla' (unconsciousness) by establishing that the obligation to make up (qada) prayer is tied to the duration of actual consciousness, rather than the entire illness period. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that the sick are exempt from prayer only while their faculties are fully impaired, ensuring that the divine command is fulfilled proportionally to the individual's capacity. This ruling underscores the balance between ease (rukhas) and obligation in Shia legal theory.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, and Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said,

‘I asked himasws about the sick one who was unconscious. Then he awoke. How would he fulfil his (missed out) Salāts?’ Heasws said: ‘He would only fulfil the Salāt at the time for which he became conscious’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hassan has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from abu Basir who has said the following:

“I once asked one of the two Imam, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, about a patient who faints and then gains consciousness, if he is required to perform his Salah (prayer) again. He (the Imam) said, ‘He is required to perform only those Salah (prayer) again for which there was still time after his gaining consciousness.’”
